evidence.claim: The organisation states on its own site that it accepts zakat and holds it as a trust rather than as income.
evidence.quote: We accept zakat and we treat it as a trust, not as income.

evidence.claim: The narrative refers to the organisation's own published zakat policy governing the administrative share it takes from zakat.
evidence.quote: We do not use zakat funds for our own operating costs beyond the administrative share permitted, which we cap at one eighth in line with our published zakat policy.

evidence.claim: The organisation publishes a stated administrative share it takes from zakat received and reports its actual figure for the year.
evidence.quote: Administrative share. We take no more than one eighth of zakat received to cover the cost of collecting and distributing it, consistent with the majority position. In the 2025-26 year our actual figure was 9.1%.

evidence.claim: The organisation states zakat is held in a designated account and never pooled with general donations or used for unrestricted costs.
evidence.quote: Every pound of zakat you give is held in a designated zakat account. It is never pooled with general donations and never used to cover unrestricted costs.

evidence.claim: The campaign narrative repeats that all zakat funds sit in a designated account separate from general donations.
evidence.quote: Amanah Relief Trust holds all zakat funds in a designated account separate from general donations.

evidence.claim: The organisation states that every household is screened against the categories of eligible zakat recipients before any zakat is disbursed.
evidence.quote: Eligibility screening. Before any zakat is disbursed, the receiving household is screened against the categories of eligible recipients.

evidence.claim: The attached assessment document describes a separate zakat screen testing nisab and non-duplication with other zakat distributors.
evidence.quote: Zakat screen. Applied separately. Confirms the household holds assets below nisab and is not in receipt of zakat from another distributing body in the same period.

evidence.claim: The narrative states zakat goes only to households confirmed eligible under a zakat screening applied on top of the poverty assessment.
evidence.quote: Zakat is disbursed only to households confirmed eligible under our zakat screening, which is applied in addition to the poverty assessment.

evidence.claim: The campaign is unconditional cash assistance to 240 households displaced by flooding, which is direct support to poor individuals.
evidence.quote: We are raising unconditional cash assistance for 240 of those households through the winter.

evidence.claim: The beneficiary population is households displaced from their villages by flooding along the Indus.
evidence.quote: Flooding across northern Sindh in June displaced roughly 11,000 households from villages along the Indus.

evidence.claim: Eligibility is tied to falling below the district poverty line, matching the sufficiency-threshold framing of the selected category.
evidence.quote: To qualify, a household must have lost its primary dwelling or its main income source, and must fall below the district poverty line as measured by our means test.

evidence.claim: A fixed cash amount goes to each individual household in three monthly transfers through a named local partner.
evidence.quote: Each household receives PKR 98,000 across three monthly transfers, delivered by our local partner Sindh Rural Support Network.

evidence.claim: Households are individually selected and signed off by named caseworkers, with a sample re-verified.
evidence.quote: Caseworker signature and date required. Ten per cent of completed assessments are re-verified by a second caseworker.

evidence.claim: The organisation concedes it retains up to one eighth of zakat received to cover its own collection and distribution costs, so not all zakat reaches households.
evidence.quote: We do not use zakat funds for our own operating costs beyond the administrative share permitted, which we cap at one eighth

evidence.claim: The organisation's filed accounts show a portion of total expenditure going to fundraising rather than charitable activity.
evidence.quote: Total expenditure GBP 3.9m, of which charitable activities GBP 3.5m and raising funds GBP 0.3m.

evidence.claim: The charity's registered objects are relief of poverty among persons in need through grants, goods and services.
evidence.quote: Objects: The relief of poverty and financial hardship among persons in need, in the United Kingdom and overseas, in particular through the provision of grants, goods and services.

evidence.claim: Households are selected by partner caseworkers using a standard intake assessment.
evidence.quote: Households are selected by SRSN caseworkers using our standard intake assessment.

evidence.claim: The assessment applies a numeric scoring threshold combined with an income test against the district poverty line.
evidence.quote: Scoring. Households scoring 4 or above and reporting monthly income below PKR 32,000 (district poverty line) are eligible.

evidence.claim: The intake form captures displacement status, income, dependants and lost productive assets.
evidence.quote: Section 2 — Income. Primary earner occupation before displacement. Current monthly household income (PKR). Number of dependants.

evidence.claim: A documented vulnerability weighting prioritises widow-headed households, disability and young children.
evidence.quote: Section 4 — Vulnerability weighting. Widow-headed household (+2). Household member with disability (+2). Children under 5 (+1 each, max +3). No adult male earner (+1).

evidence.claim: The narrative states outright that the transfer is a grant with nothing repaid and nothing asked in return.
evidence.quote: This is a grant. Nothing is repaid, and no household is asked for anything in return.

evidence.claim: The assistance is described as unconditional cash rather than in-kind or conditional support.
evidence.quote: Cash rather than in-kind because the district markets are functioning and families consistently tell us they need different things — some school fees, some medicine, some replacing a lost livestock animal.
